prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which designed bifunctional small molecules bring a target protein and a ubiquitin ligase together so that the target is ubiquitinated and removed by the proteasome

statement.case_for: I keep B056 with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli. The discovery is a single chemical principle: a designed molecule forms a ternary complex that makes ubiquitination of a chosen protein event-driven and catalytic. Crews and Deshaies set out and first demonstrated it in 2001. Ciulli's crystal structures of VHL with its ligands and of degrader ternary complexes, with the cooperativity analysis, explain why some degraders work and others do not, and let degraders be designed rather than found by screening. That is the kind of evidence I trust, because the mechanism rests on determined structures. The principle has been reproduced independently by many laboratories on many target classes. Round 1 showed seven of eight members converging on this ballot, and no one disputed the principle itself, so my remaining task is to decide the third seat and the wording on the merits, not to count votes.
statement.case_against: The reservation I take most seriously is that no degrader is yet a broadly approved drug, and I am recalling trial status, not verifying it, so the citation must rest on the chemical principle and the mechanism and not on therapeutic promise. The second is that a Ciulli trio leaves the cereblon and molecular-glue strand (Handa, Ito) unnamed, and that strand is a separate datable discovery that explains the clinically most advanced degraders. In round 1 my citation mentioned molecular glues while naming no glue discoverer; I have removed that wording so the citation describes what the three named people did. Sakamoto's co-authorship of the 2001 paper is also a real attribution question that three seats cannot settle.

responses.point: Linke shares my Ciulli trio and would add 'induced proximity to ubiquitin ligases' to the wording so that the glue strand fits, while saying he could be persuaded that cereblon was the more decisive original step.
responses.response: I would not add induced-proximity wording if Handa is not named, because it would let the citation claim a glue strand whose discoverers we leave out. That is the inconsistency I found in my own round-1 text. Either the citation is about designed bifunctional molecules and the trio is Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, or it covers both strands and Handa has to be named. On your question of which step was more decisive: cereblon explained an existing drug, whereas the PROTAC principle plus structure-guided ligand and ternary-complex design is what generalised to any target. I remain on the principle, and I would take the cereblon route only if the expert report shows that most clinical degraders depend on it in a way that outweighs the design framework.

responses.point: Aili wants Handa as the third name so that one citation covers both PROTACs and cereblon glues, and would not split B056 into separate parts.
responses.response: A single unified citation is attractive, and I have not found a scientific argument that the glue strand is less important. My disagreement is about what the three seats should reward. Handa's contribution is a target identification for an old drug; the Ciulli work is a structural and quantitative basis that transfers to new targets, which is the part of the field I can evaluate directly. I will not insist on this beyond the final ballot, but I would ask Aili to say which of Crews, Deshaies or Handa would move if the committee decided to include Ciulli as well, since a trio that drops Ciulli drops the structural basis of drug-like PROTACs from the record.

responses.point: Brzezinski asks that the expert report show how much of the ternary-complex framework is attributable to Ciulli and not shared with the Crews laboratory.
responses.response: That is the right test and I can give a structural view of it. The Crews group established the PROTAC concept and cell-permeable VHL-based molecules, but the VHL ligand structures, the crystal structures of VHL-PROTAC-target ternary complexes and the cooperativity measurements that explain selectivity came from the Ciulli laboratory, and they are what made rational design possible. I would still want the expert report to check priority dates for the VHL ligand work against the Crews laboratory's own ligand development. If that check shows heavy overlap, my case for Ciulli over Handa weakens, and I say so openly.

responses.point: Somfai remains alone on B051 (Buchwald and Hartwig), arguing that C-N coupling is as distinct from the 2010 prize as Suzuki is from Heck, and says he would move toward B056 if the committee prefers a modality.
responses.response: I grant that C-N coupling needed its own ligand logic and that the argument on amine binding and reductive elimination is real, so I withdraw the suggestion that it is only a refinement. My difficulty remains that the 2010 prize honoured palladium catalysis for bond formation as a concept, and Kosugi's precedent leaves a priority question for a two-person prize. I do not rank it above B056 this year, but if B056 fails to reach a majority I would take B051 seriously as a second part, with the citation resting on the catalyst design and not on adoption.

uncertainties: Whether the expert report shows that the VHL ligand and ternary-complex work was distinct enough from the Crews laboratory to justify Ciulli over Handa.
Whether the committee prefers to name the cereblon strand through Handa, in which case I would accept Handa and the citation would need to cover both strands.
Whether Sakamoto, as 2001 co-author, has a claim that should displace a seat.
Whether the absence of an approved degrader makes B056 premature, a point I cannot verify from memory.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any B056 name. I work on zeolites and porous frameworks and know Jihong Yu and Michael Tsapatsis (B059) professionally, so I would recuse from deciding on B059 if it advanced; B059 is only an alternative of mine. I am a Stockholm University colleague of the Secretary, Peter Brzezinski, which is not a conflict for any shortlisted candidate.
